transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-17
Start: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Atlas ML), Samantha Ortiz (Atlas Infra), Marcus Hale (Atlas CTO), Lina Park (Atlas Product)

Summary:
Quick POC sync to review last week's tuning (continuous batching changes and queue sizing), throughput numbers from the benchmark, and agree next steps for the pilot. Tension between p95 latency SLO and maximizing tokens/sec; exploring concurrency targets and short queueing windows.

[00:00] Alex: ok hey everyone thanks for joining, can you hear me?
[00:05] Jordan: yep loud and clear, thanks Alex
[00:08] Alex: cool quick agenda - recap of last run, priya will walk through the new continuous batching configs, then we compare numbers, then action items. any additions?
[00:18] Samantha: just curious if we'll talk about queueing thresholds, that's what caused the spike last week.
[00:22] Alex: yep we'll cover that.

[02:15] Priya: alright so last week we turned on continuous batching at the runtime level and set the batch_collect window to 8ms and max_batch_size 64. we also enabled prefix KV caching for cold-start reduction but note the k-v cash was a bit noisy in the traces, sometimes key misses were high.
[02:40] Marcus: sorry what do you mean by k-v cash? is that the cache on the GPU or the serving layer?
[02:46] Priya: it's the KV cache in the model runner - stores cached attention key/values across streams. that reduced token compute on repeated prefixes. However, if your traffic has high variance in prefixes the cache hit drops. Jordan can probably speak to that.
[03:06] Jordan: yeah a lot of our requests are user messages with unique ids and prompts so hits are modest, around 15-20% for the demo set, but in production we might get higher reuse for system prompts.

[05:00] Priya: ok numbers - baseline (no continuous batching, concurrency 1) we measured 120 tokens/sec per GPU and p95 latency ~210ms for 512-token responses. with continuous batching and max_batch_size 64 we got aggregate throughput up to ~950 tokens/sec when we allowed concurrency 4 and a small queue window of 20ms. p95 latency moved to ~260ms in that config.
[05:30] Samantha: that 260ms p95 is a concern, our product team wants <200ms 95th in steady state.
[05:35] Lina: yes 200ms is the target for our real-time feature, but we can be flexible during the pilot if throughput improvement offsets cost.

[07:10] Priya: there are tradeoffs - continuous batching increases GPU utilization and amortizes attention compute across multiple requests which gives tokens/sec gains but introduces queuing latency. We tried tightening queue windows to 10ms and that brought p95 down to ~220ms but reduced throughput to ~700 tokens/sec.
[07:35] Diego: another lever is concurrency - if you increase replicas and run concurrency 2 per GPU you can keep queue windows small and still hit higher aggregate QPS. example: 2 replicas with concurrency 2 each and batch_size limit 48, queue window 12ms gave ~820 tokens/sec and p95 ~205ms.

[09:00] Marcus: what's the cost delta between adding concurrency vs going to dedicated GPUs?
[09:06] Alex: rough rule - increasing concurrency or replicas increases vCPU and memory usage on the node and may increase infra cost but keeps you on hosted. Dedicated reserved capacity adds committed monthly costs but reduces per-token price. I'll send a pricing CSV with scenarios after this call.

[11:45] Jordan: on the sample workload we also saw that quantization from fp16 -> int8 had minimal quality impact but improved inference kernel throughput by ~15% in our synthetic run. is Redwood recommending quantization in pilot?
[11:58] Priya: yes we have quantization profiles we suggest; int8 or 4-bit profiles depend on model family. for this model the int8 path looks safe but we'll validate against your eval prompts.

[13:20] Samantha: security question - if we go with dedicated or private, how does key management work? do you support bring-your-own-kms?
[13:29] Alex: yes BYOK supported for Private; Dedicated can integrate with customer KMS for key wrap. I'll attach the SOC 2 and security spreadsheet in the follow-up.

[15:45] Priya: back to tuning - queueing strategy options: 1) micro-batching short queue windows (8-15ms) + higher concurrency 2) slightly larger window (20-30ms) single replica to maximize batch sizes 3) adaptive windowing (we can enable a dynamic queue that shrinks during spikes). Option 3 is experimental but we can enable in a canary.

[17:02] Jordan: I like option 1 since we want steady p95. what's the expected effect on cold starts?
[17:10] Diego: micro-batching has less batching buildup so cold-starts are more visible per request; but prefix caching helps reduce the compute once warmed. You can also pre-warm a small pool of workers.

[19:20] Priya: we also instrumented request-size based routing - heavy long responses can be routed to a separate pool tuned for long-form generation which avoids polluting the short-response latency pool.

[22:00] Samantha: ok can you explain the concurrency sweep you mentioned?
[22:05] Priya: sure we tested concurrency = 1,2,4,8 with fixed batch window 12ms and max_batch_size 64. results were non-linear - concurrency 1 gave stable 120 tok/s (per GPU) per baseline; concurrency 2 gave 380 tok/s aggregate; concurrency 4 gave 650 tok/s but p95 jumped; concurrency 8 gave marginal throughput gain and much higher tail latency. so there is a sweet spot around 2-4 for your workload.

[25:40] Marcus: are there scheduler knobs to limit queue depth so single requests don't wait too long behind heavy bursts?
[25:46] Priya: yes we have an enforced max_queue_ms and per-request SLA cutoff - if request would be delayed beyond threshold it can either run standalone or be dropped back to a lower-cost fallback model. we can set this to 30ms for your low-latency route.

[28:10] Jordan: about the fallback model, does Redwood support automatic fallback to cheaper model if primary overloaded?
[28:16] Alex: yes routing policies can fallback to compatible variants; you can set cost vs quality thresholds. it's part of the rollout config.

[30:00] Priya: quick note - the last run's logs showed some noisy transcription in the traces where the runner reported sporadic kernel stalls tied to our older CUDA on that node. we recommended updating driver + runtime. Samantha, can you confirm the infra kernel/drivers?
[30:20] Samantha: we're on CUDA 11.6 on those test instances; we can schedule an update but need to coordinate maintenance window.

[32:00] Diego: that explains the throughput jitter. with updated drivers and optimized kernels you should see ~8-10% uplift on the same config.

[33:40] Jordan: what's the plan for production rollout if we pick micro-batching + concurrency 2?
[33:46] Alex: plan: pilot tuning (this week) -> run 48hr stability test with traffic replay -> compare p95 and cost metrics -> if stable, do small canary in prod region and ramp. we'll provide runbook and monitoring dashboards.

[36:00] Lina: for product we need a clear success metric - can we define success as achieve >=750 tokens/sec with p95 <=200ms for 95% of test windows?
[36:10] Priya: yes we can target that but will need concurrency=2 replicas and queue window ~12ms and maybe int8 quantization.

[38:20] Marcus: final question on billing - if we run concurrency and multiple replicas for the pilot, will we be charged per replica or per GPU-min?
[38:28] Alex: hosted pricing is per vCPU/GPU minute plus per-token; dedicated is committed capacity monthly. I'll model both and show delta for the pilot config.

[40:00] Alex: ok recap - Priya to run the concurrency sweep and micro-batching tests and post results, Jordan to share traffic traces and avg seq len, Alex to send pricing and security docs, Diego to join next week for latency deep-dive. agreed?
[40:14] All: yep

[41:00] Jordan: one more tiny thing - we'll also share a set of eval prompts to verify quantization quality.
[41:10] Priya: great, we'll run evals against the int8 profile and put difference metrics into the spreadsheet.

[43:00] Alex: thanks everyone, we'll follow-up with the spreadsheet and schedule the next sync for 2026-03-24 same time.
[43:10] Samantha: thanks all
[43:15] Marcus: thanks

End of call.

References:
- Benchmark sheet: link to /sheets/pilot-throughput-2026-03 (shared in CRM)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings (k-v cash for KV cache), speaker overlap at ~22:05, some numeric rounding in throughput numbers.
